CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right leg pain.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Mrs. Peterson is a 43-year-old patient who presents with right leg pain sustained during a bowling incident. She reports that while running up to the lane with her bowling ball pulled back, she swung the ball forward and struck her right leg instead of the lane, causing her to fall. She denies significant swelling but reports some bruising on the back of her leg. She has been able to walk only minimally and with difficulty. She reports the leg is very sore with weight-bearing. She would avoid stairs at all costs. She has been taking ibuprofen and acetaminophen for pain management.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Not discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Atopic eczema.
Diverticulosis with history of diverticulitis, status post colectomy with partial colon removal.

MEDICATIONS
Fluocinonide for eczema as needed when itchy.
Ibuprofen and acetaminophen as needed for current leg pain.

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient bowls recreationally.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Significant tenderness to the lateral aspect of the right upper leg. No pain or tenderness with flexion or extension of the lower leg.

RESULTS
X-ray of right femur: Normal. No evidence of fracture or swelling.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Right leg contusion. Start mobic 15 milligrams once daily for anti-inflammatory effect. Ice for pain management. Expected improvement within one week. Patient instructed to return if symptoms do not improve.
